title: Layouts
subject: ui
summary: How to compose page structure using shared layout components and compositions.

purpose.intro: How to compose page structure using shared layout components and compositions.

claims.text: **Columns** (`LeftSidebar`, `RightSidebar`, `ContextPanel`, `Main`) — width is set by the theme (`Main` takes what is left), height grows to the parent's max.
**Containers** (`PageBody`, `MainBody`) — flex rows that fill the remaining height after their header sibling. They carry their own structural defaults; you do not need to add sizing classes to them.
**`ScrollArea`** — the only element that scrolls. Everything else has `overflow: hidden`. Always place a `ScrollArea` wherever content needs to scroll; never add `overflow: auto/scroll` ad-hoc.

reference.statement: **Rows** (`PageHeader`, `SecondPageHeader`, `MainHeader`, `SecondMainHeader`) — height is set by the theme, width grows to fill the parent.

claims.text: Overlays (Dialog, Sheet) are handled by the component library as `element="overlay--*"` surfaces, not layout regions. They are independent of the page tree.

reference.statement: Every structural region carries a `layout` attribute. A div is **either** `layout` or `element`, never both. The theme engine styles `layout` regions (background, border, etc.) the same way it styles `element` surfaces — the layout components never emit visual CSS themselves.

claims.text: **shell-side-nav**
**shell-none**
MINIMAL PAGE
**Mental model:**
**Cols** (ShellNav, sidebars, ContextPanel, MainBody): `width` set by theme, height fills parent (`align-self: stretch` or `flex: 1`)
**Rows** (Shell, Page, PageBody, Main, MainContent): `height` set by theme or fills parent (`flex: 1`), width is always `100%`
**Fixed edges** (PageHeader, SecondPageHeader, MainHeader, SecondMainHeader, MainFooter): `flex-shrink: 0` — they never shrink; the remaining space goes to MainContent
All structural flex defaults are **engine-hardcoded** — not theme-overridable. Theme controls surfaces, widths, and heights only.

The `page` region sits inside the shell content area. `page-body` is the flex row. `second-page-header` and `second-main-header` are optional: a second row under the page header (e.g. the tabs of the page) and under the main header. Use them in order, never alone: no second row without the first. `main-header` spans the full width of the `main` column — it is NOT inside `left-sidebar` or `right-sidebar`.
`right-sidebar` and `context-panel` can coexist — the flex layout handles both simultaneously (e.g. activity feed + properties panel).

claims.text: The structural behaviour it encapsulates (`flex: 1 / min-height: 0 / overflow-y: auto`) is a constant source of broken layouts when reinvented ad-hoc. Using `ScrollArea` everywhere means this is always correct and the theme applies consistent scrollbar styling automatically.
The theme controls scrollbar appearance via `[layout="scroll-area"]`.

**Constraint:** `ScrollArea` must be inside a flex parent (row or column) to size correctly. `flex-1 min-h-0` only takes effect inside a flex container. All natural parents in the layout tree are flex containers, so this is always satisfied. If you ever place it inside a non-flex container, give it an explicit height instead.

reference.statement: `scroll-area` is the canonical way to make any container internally scrollable. Use it anywhere a region needs to scroll — inside a card, a sidebar, a dialog, a panel, the main body. It is not tied to the page tree.

snippets.code:
// inside a card
<Card>
  <CardHeader>…</CardHeader>
  <ScrollArea>
    <LongList />
  </ScrollArea>
</Card>

// inside a sidebar
<LeftSidebar>
  <NavHeader />
  <ScrollArea>
    <NavItems />
  </ScrollArea>
</LeftSidebar>

claims.text: It replaces hand-rolled `flex` markup. Where a developer would write `flex items-center justify-between gap-3` and give a child `flex-1 min-w-0`, they write a Stack and give the child `position="fill"`. The structural rules that break most often when reinvented — the `min-width: 0` overflow fix on a growing child, mixing row and column nesting — are encoded once.
Sizing is Figma's vocabulary, set on the child:

A non-Stack child (a Card, a span) takes the same behaviour through its `position` attribute: `position="fill"` to fill, `position="hug"` to hug (markup-dictionary.md § Position). The structural utilities (`flex-1 min-w-0`, `flex-none`) still work and are on their way out.

Stack emits `layout="stack"` and `data-dir`. It sets no colour, border, radius or shadow — those belong to the theme and to the content components placed inside. Gap and padding are applied inline because they are arbitrary structural values, not visual ones.

`Stack` is the one primitive that takes spacing from markup: `gap` and `pad`, as a number (px) or a CSS length. No other primitive or component takes a spacing or size number; their spacing and dimensions come from the theme. `className` and inline `style` are deprecated and are not used for spacing.

**When not to use it:** when cells must align across both axes at once — a bento dashboard where the columns of row 2 line up with those of row 1. Stack is one-dimensional per level; that case is a grid: give the parent `position="cols-N"` and each child `position="span-N"` (markup-dictionary.md § Position). Never the `grid` utilities.

reference.statement: `stack` is the auto-layout primitive: one box that is a row or a column and owns the gap, the alignment and the padding between its children. Children own only their content. A non-uniform composition — a header over two columns over a footer, a label beside a number beside an action — is nested stacks; a "cell" is another Stack. It is usable inside any region and is not tied to the page tree.

imagesAndDiagrams.value:
| Prop | Values | Default | Notes |
|------|--------|---------|-------|
| `dir` | `"row"` `"col"` | `"col"` | Main axis |
| `gap` | `number` (px) or a CSS length | — | Space between children |
| `align` | `"start"` `"center"` `"end"` `"stretch"` `"baseline"` | `stretch` (browser default) | Cross-axis alignment |
| `justify` | `"start"` `"center"` `"end"` `"between"` `"around"` | `start` (browser default) | Main-axis distribution |
| `wrap` | `boolean` | `false` | Children flow onto new lines (a cluster) |
| `size` | `"hug"` `"fill"` `"fixed"` | `"hug"` | How this Stack sizes inside its parent Stack |
| `pad` | `number` (px) or a CSS length | — | Inner padding |

| Size | Behaviour | Flex |
|------|-----------|------|
| `hug` | As small as its content | `flex: none` |
| `fill` | Grows into the leftover space; may shrink below content size | `flex: 1 1 0; min-width/height: 0` |
| `fixed` | Keeps its own width/height: the theme's (a field, an avatar) or, for a non-Stack child, a `position` width (`w-xs`…`w-xl`) | `flex: none` |

reference.statement: Every region takes `position` like any surface (markup-dictionary.md § Position): `fill`, `hug`, `start` `center` `end` `stretch`, `clip`, `w-xs`…`w-xl`, `cols-N` / `span-N`. The region's own dimension (a sidebar's width, a header's height) stays the theme's; `position` says where it stands in its parent and how much it takes.

reference.topic: Ownership › Layout components handle structural behavior only
reference.statement: Scroll, overflow, collapse, breakpoints, sticky positioning. They render `layout="..."` attributes. They know nothing about content or visual appearance. The theme engine handles visuals.
A module page never builds its own shell or makes structural decisions. It imports a shared composition and fills the slots.

snippets.caption: tsx

claims.text: **`layout` or `element`, never both.** A div is the structural frame OR the morphological surface inside it. Never mix them.
**Layout components own all structural decisions.** Scroll, overflow, collapse, breakpoints, sticky. Page authors fill slots — they never write structural CSS.
**The theme engine styles layout regions.** `layout="left-sidebar"` gets background, border, width from the theme. The layout component itself emits no visual CSS.
**`main-header` spans the full `main` column.** It is not inside `left-sidebar`. It is a full-width region at the top of `main`, sitting above `main-body`.
**Modules never build their own shell or navigation.** They consume shared compositions.

reference.topic: Public surface (`@prowd/ui/layouts`) › Compositions (recommended for module pages)

claims.text: `StandardPage`, `FullPage` and `SplitPage` are not built yet; pages compose the primitives directly until they are.
